title: A list item with a wide marker and a nested list that needs wrapping is left unformatted
description:
`yamark format --wrap sentence` returns a list item unchanged when the item has a wide marker (`*   `, `-   `, `1.  `) and a nested list item whose text needs wrapping.

Reproduced on 0.4.0 and 0.5.0.

## Repro

```md
*   Outer.

    - Nested. Second
      wrapped.
```

```
yamark format --wrap sentence --diff repro.md
```

Expected: the item is reformatted like its neighbors, or the file is reported as skipped or failed.
Actual: no diff, and the summary reads `1 files scanned, 0 formatted, 1 unchanged, 0 skipped, 0 failed`.

## What does and does not trigger it

| Outer marker | Nested list text | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `- ` | needs wrapping | formatted |
| `*   ` | already one sentence per line | formatted, marker becomes `- ` |
| `*   ` | needs wrapping | **unchanged** |
| `1.  ` | needs wrapping | **unchanged** |

The skip applies to the item, not the list.
Sibling items in the same list are still formatted:

```md
*   First.

    - Nested. Second
      wrapped.

*   Other. Second
    wrapped.
```

Only `Other. Second wrapped.` is rewritten.
The nested list's marker width doesn't matter (`- ` and `-   ` behave the same), and neither does whether a blank line separates it from the outer paragraph.

title: A list item with a paragraph after a fenced code block is left unformatted
description:
`yamark format --wrap sentence` returns a list item unchanged when the item contains a paragraph after a fenced code block. The text before the fence is not wrapped either, so the whole item is skipped. The summary reports `0 skipped, 0 failed`.

Reproduced on 0.4.0 and 0.5.0. The marker is an ordinary `- `, and there is no nested list.

This looks related to #26.

## Repro

````md
- Item. Second
  wrapped.

  ```
  code
  ```

  After.
````

```
yamark format --wrap sentence --diff repro.md
```

Expected: `Item. Second wrapped.` becomes `Item.` / `Second wrapped.`.
Actual: no diff, and the summary reads `1 files scanned, 0 formatted, 1 unchanged, 0 skipped, 0 failed`.

## What does and does not trigger it

| Content of the list item | Result |
|---|---|
| paragraph, fence | formatted |
| paragraph, fence, nested list | formatted |
| paragraph, fence, second fence | formatted |
| paragraph, fence, **paragraph** | **unchanged** |
| fence, **paragraph** | **unchanged** |

The same constructs formatted as plain top-level content, or inside a block quote, are formatted normally. The skip applies to the item: sibling items in the same list are still formatted.

The fence's language, and the amount of text after the fence, make no difference. My runs used `--wrap sentence --skip-embedded-formatters`.

title: Panic on non-breaking spaces
description:
We had a document with some stray non-breaking spaces. Yamark 0.4.0 ignored them but 0.5.0 actually crashes.

This doesn't block us because the non-breaking spaces were added to the file by accident, but still, it's probably good to know about crash bugs.

## Repro

```
printf -- '- Item.\n \xc2\xa0Continuation line.\n' > repro.md
yamark format --wrap sentence --diff repro.md
```

Output:

```
thread 'main' panicked at src/core/markdown/containers.rs:167:53:
start byte index 2 is not a char boundary; it is inside '\u{a0}' (bytes 1..3 of string)
```

It also panics when the line is a separate paragraph in the item (`printf -- '- Item.\n\n \xc2\xa0Continuation paragraph.\n'`). It does not panic for the same two lines outside a list.

title: CRLF code fence: closing fence ends up on the last code line after Python formatting
description:
With CRLF line endings, formatting a Python fence through the built-in `ruff` formatter puts the closing fence on the last code line, which breaks the document.

````md
```python
x = sum(range(10))
x
```
````

(saved with CRLF line endings)

```
yamark format repro.md
```

The file ends up with `x\r` directly followed by the closing backticks, so the fence is never closed and the rest of the document becomes code. Git also sees the file as binary afterwards because of the lone CR. The same file with LF line endings formats fine. I can reproduce with yamark 0.4.0 and ruff 0.17.1 on Windows, with both `python` and Quarto `{python}` fences.

From what I can tell, ruff in notebook mode drops only the final `\n` of the cell source and keeps the `\r` before it:

```
CRLF cell source in:  "import sys, platform\r\nx = 1\r\nx\r\n"
ruff cell source out: ["import sys, platform\r\n", "\r\n", "x = 1\r\n", "x\r"]
LF cell source out:   ["import sys, platform\n", "\n", "x = 1\n", "x"]
```

Then the check that restores a missing final line ending looks like it treats a trailing `\r` as a complete line ending, so nothing is added before the closing fence:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/emit.rs#L447-L450

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/emit.rs#L751-L755

A trailing `\r` is a valid line ending for a CR-only document, but probably not when the fence opening uses `\r\n`. Please correct me if I'm reading it wrong. Happy to help test on Windows if useful.

title: Sentence wrap in list items can start a line with a list marker
description:
With `--wrap sentence`, a list item paragraph can be split right before a token that reads as a list marker, so the next sentence becomes a nested list.

```md
- Options: (a) keep it. (b) drop it.
- Steps: first. - second.
- Version 1.12 ships now. 2. Later.
```

```
yamark format --wrap sentence repro.md
```

Output:

```md
- Options: (a) keep it.
  (b) drop it.
- Steps: first.
  - second.
- Version 1.12 ships now.
  2.
  Later.
```

Pandoc parses `(b) drop it.` and `- second.` as nested lists here. With `--wrap 72` the same inputs keep the marker away from the line start, and a top-level single-line paragraph is left unchanged, so the guard exists. It looks like plain sentence mode does not enable it:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/wrap.rs#L3046-L3066

and the paragraph-level check only runs for top-level paragraphs, and only when the source paragraph was a single line:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/wrap.rs#L33-L34

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/wrap/plan.rs#L346-L356

A related case: a top-level paragraph that spans several source lines, like `Intro line\ncontinues. Pick one. - other thing.`, comes out with `- other thing.` at a line start. Pandoc markdown keeps that as a paragraph, but CommonMark reads it as a list.

Is the guard meant to apply to sentence mode too ?

title: Paragraph after a nested list is moved out of its list item when wrapping
description:
A paragraph that continues a list item after a nested list is emitted at column 0, so it leaves the list and the following items start a new list.

```md
- Item with a nested list:
  - nested one
  - nested two

  Paragraph that continues the outer item.
- Next item.
```

```
yamark format --wrap sentence repro.md
```

Output:

```md
- Item with a nested list:
  - nested one
  - nested two

Paragraph that continues the outer item.
- Next item.
```

Same result with `--wrap 72`. `--wrap none` keeps the input unchanged. Without the nested list (blank line then the indented paragraph), the paragraph stays in the item. A nested blockquote or code fence instead of the nested list is also fine. Line endings don't matter here.

From what I can tell, the list block ends at the blank line because only the content indent of the most recent item is tracked. After `  - nested two` it becomes 4, so the paragraph at indent 2 (the outer item's content column) no longer counts as a continuation:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/markdown.rs#L2583-L2616

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/ff3160b5e7b4a5a74d710295951408be58e201e4/src/core/markdown.rs#L2628-L2634

The paragraph is then formatted as a top-level paragraph. Does that match your understanding?

title: Sentence wrap skipped for whole paragraph when {{ }} appears anywhere in it, even inside inline code
description:
A paragraph containing a literal `{{ ... }}` sequence is copied verbatim instead of being wrapped, even when the `{{ ... }}` is inside inline code and would never be touched by the reflow itself.

```md
First
sentence with `${{ foo }}`. Second
sentence.
```

```
yamark format --wrap sentence repro.md --diff
```

Output: unchanged. Removing one of the braces (`${ foo }`) makes wrapping work again, and it also reproduces with no code span at all (`{{ foo }}` in plain text).

From what I can tell, this comes from the default template delimiters (`{{ }}`, `{% %}`, `{# #}`, `<% %>`) documented here:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/b0bc600d1fb79a4d2b8bf6a1bd8a306da96b84c6/website/reference-config.html.md#L32-L36

and enforced at emission time here, independent of the plan chosen for the node:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/b0bc600d1fb79a4d2b8bf6a1bd8a306da96b84c6/src/core/emit.rs#L126

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/b0bc600d1fb79a4d2b8bf6a1bd8a306da96b84c6/src/core/emit.rs#L572-L587

The underlying scan looks like a plain substring search with no code-span awareness:

https://github.com/t-kalinowski/yamark/blob/b0bc600d1fb79a4d2b8bf6a1bd8a306da96b84c6/src/core/directives.rs#L44-L72

So a `{{ ... }}` anywhere in the paragraph, including inside backticks, forces the whole paragraph to be copied raw instead of just protecting the delimited span itself.

The doc says the delimiters exist to avoid mangling the *content* of a template region. Disabling wrap for the whole surrounding paragraph seems broader than that, especially once the span is already inert inside inline code. Is that the intended scope of `[template]`, or would code-span-aware detection (skip the check for `{{ }}` already inside backticks) be in scope? Happy to help test on Windows if useful.
